reasoning_trace.value: The paper proposes a MIMO-radar based cyclist detection method for long-range scenarios using Integrated Sensing And Communication (ISAC). The method employs Capon and amplitude and phase estimation (APES) beamforming techniques to estimate the angle of arrival (AoA) of the target. The paper includes several figures and tables to illustrate the simulation results and performance of the proposed method.

The paper introduces the concept of ISAC and its application in long-range cyclist detection. It highlights the challenges of low Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) conditions and proposes the use of MIMO radar and beamforming techniques to address these challenges. The paper also discusses the system model, including the transmitter and receiver antenna arrays, and the target state matrix.

The paper presents simulation results to evaluate the performance of the proposed method. The results show that the Capon beamformer provides accurate angle estimation but suffers from limited resolution, while the APES beamformer offers superior resolution at the cost of estimation accuracy. The paper also presents Monte-Carlo simulation results to evaluate the detection performance of the proposed method.

The paper identifies the limitations of the proposed method, including the reduced angular resolution of the Capon beamformer and the bias in the estimated angles of the APES beamformer. The paper suggests future work to develop methods that enhance angular resolution while reducing estimation bias.
